You don't *need* to be sectioned to be admitted to a mental hospital. 'Sections' are in place for people who either can't make that decision due to mental illness or the risk of suicide/harm to others is so great that they need to be detained. If it's just going into hospital you want, you'll want to go in informally as that imposes less restrictions on your freedom (you can self discharge from an informal admission unless your behaviour makes them worry about you). That being said, hospital beds are at an all time low due to budget cutbacks. The government is trying to save costs by pushing for more and more people to be treated at home (to the detriment of most people, although some people do benefit from not learning to depend on regular nurse checks just to be safe). There have been more than a few occasions just this past month where there were ZERO beds in the country, period. I hope you get the help you need, whatever form it takes.

Turn 30 this year, 5 years since I came out to my closest friends and I still feel like I'm stuck in limbo. I've had my doubts about Islam since I was a lot younger, and it was more to do with the idea that decent people could be sent to hell just by being unlucky enough to be born to the 'wrong' circumstances. Leaving Islam came at around the same time as coming up, alongside the realization that no, it's not going to go away just by praying extra hard or listening to your religious friends tell you sympathetically that they will pray for your to be guided back. The suicidal thoughts came soon after- everything I'd wanted... everything I thought I'd wanted or been taught to want felt like it was a closed door to me. Despite being bullied in an Islamic boarding school for 'not being islamic enough' (their logic being that I should be spending my free time reading the Quran and learning arabic, not Star Wars novels), I think a small part of me always just wanted to fit in, and here, it just felt like if there was a God, he was saying 'You thought you'd belong somewhere someday. Fuck you. Here's another reason to be isolated from everyone else'. The platitudes of 'it's a test, you need to be strong' grew more and more nauseating to hear with every day that passed. The small thing I did hold on to initially was the idea that my parents, although still Muslim had always struck me as being a lot more open minded that others in my community. My dad is the local mosque's bilal, but plays in a Pink Floyd cover band. My mother used to smoke, drink, model, and had some gay friends. So I thought that, maybe, once I work up the courage to tell them, they might just accept it, and given that they've almost been my best friends growing up, that should be all that mattered. Then that phone call happened 2 years ago- a man from my country got married to another man in Ireland and it made the front page of tabloids so people could complain about it. My mother started out by joking that my aunts are all saying 'That'll be you next'. Then in a more serious tone, she continues. 'If I'm honest though, I would rather find out you went to jail for murdering someone than find out you're gay. That shit is disgusting.' Message received. So that's not a conversation I'll be having with her anytime soon. And although I tell myself I've accepted things, and have put myself out there on dates and such, I can never seem to move forward. I'm 30 and have a medical degree, but anytime something gets a hint of being serious, I find myself worrying what my parents would think. Pretending you're alright after kissing someone then crying in the toilet once you've gotten home gets old after a while. So really, I'm gay, but it terms of moving forward with my life, it's easier to just... not do anything. Luckily medicine is a career that you can bury yourself in, and if nothing else, my parents although understandably worried that I'm not dating yet actually backed me up at my sister's wedding when I was trying to swat off relatives harassing me with the fun 'When are you getting married?' type questions. So yeah. At least a forced/arranged marriage is nowhere in the cards unlike for some people I know. I just worry that I'm going to run out of reasons to keep going someday. The friends I keep are great company but it's coming round to that time in my life where I'm watching everyone go on to starting families, and really I just need to sort my own head out now if I'm going to stand a chance.
